method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the current loop lies in the y-z plane, with +y upward, +x to the right, and the current arrow on the left/front side of the loop directed upward; the bar magnet is above the loop with its North pole on the left end. From the question text, identify that only the force on the North pole due to the loop is requested. Treat the current loop as a magnetic dipole/electromagnet: use the right-hand rule with the shown current to determine the loop’s magnetic moment direction, then use the fact that the magnetic field in the equatorial region of a dipole points opposite to the dipole moment. At the North pole’s location above the loop, this gives a magnetic field toward +x. Since a magnetic North pole feels force in the direction of the external magnetic field, the force is +x.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the loop is vertical in the y-z plane, the current direction is shown by the arrow on the left side, and the North pole of the magnet is above the loop; the +x axis points to the right. From the text, focus on the field produced by the current loop at the North pole. Apply the Biot-Savart law directly: parameterize the circular loop in the y-z plane with current direction matching the arrow. For the field point at the North pole, pair current elements symmetrically around the loop so their y and z field components cancel.
